headline: ARY books exactly Rs 0 of service income today, yet already pays 18 tailors Rs 5.77 lakh a year for a service it never bills — a Rs 6 lakh/month service stack layered onto the existing 1,018-bills-a-day footfall would add ~Rs 38.6 lakh/year of gross profit, the same as growing merchandise turnover 17.8% (Rs 1.37 Cr), because a service rupee earns ~54% against merchandise's verified 28.19%.
confidenceGap: Every ARY-side fact and both government rate cards are verified from live queries and primary PDFs, but all twelve monthly revenue figures are modelled estimates built on assumed penetration rates, not observed service demand — ARY has never sold a service, so there is no historical base to calibrate against. Compounding this, the session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) before I began, so AePS/DMT payouts, courier franchise shares, recharge margins, IRCTC agent caps and the India Post franchise scheme could not be verified against primary sources. The single largest swing factor is whether the Kalgidhar Trust already provides laundry, pharmacy and printing internally as part of hostel/school fees — if it does, roughly half the sized opportunity (laundry Rs 54k/mo + Jan Aushadhi Rs 36k/mo + part of the print counter) disappears, and nobody outside the Trust can answer that.

findings.claim: ARY earns zero service or commission income today — not a small amount, literally none. No income account carries a service balance, none of the 93 product groups is a service group, and the POS's commission field is unused on every payment mode.
findings.evidence: ary query "SELECT a.AccountID,a.AccountName,g.GroupName,a.DebitAmount,a.CreditAmount FROM AccountMaster a JOIN GroupMaster g ON g.GroupID=a.GroupID WHERE a.GroupID IN (14,15,16,29,30,31,516,526,508,512)" — the only income accounts with balances are Sales A/C, Sales Return, Discount Received, Creditors Written Off, Interest On Fdr, Other Charges, Unclaimed Balances W/O. Plus: ary query on ProductGroupMaster (93 rows, all merchandise) and ary masters payment-modes (commission_pct = 0.000 on all 11 modes).
findings.soWhat: There is no baseline to defend and no internal politics to unwind — every rupee of service revenue is additive, and the chart of accounts must be extended before anything can even be measured.

findings.claim: ARY's realised merchandise gross margin is 28.19%. This is the bar any service must beat, and services clear it by roughly 1.9x.
findings.evidence: ary query joining SaleDetail to ProductChildMaster.PurchaseCost over 2025-08-22..2026-08-21: gross_sales 77,003,742, cogs 55,299,270, gm_pct 28.19. Line coverage 1,043,344 of 1,044,180 lines = 99.92%.
findings.number: 28.19% (Rs 7.70 Cr sales, Rs 5.53 Cr COGS, Rs 2.17 Cr gross profit)
findings.soWhat: A blended ~54% service margin means Rs 38.6 L of service gross profit equals Rs 1.37 Cr of extra merchandise turnover — a 17.8% sales jump ARY would otherwise have to fight for.

findings.claim: ARY already runs a tailoring operation as a pure cost centre: 18 named tailors on a payable account, Rs 5.77 lakh paid in 2025 and Rs 3.58 lakh to Aug-2026, growing ~46% a year — with no stitching revenue account and no stitching SKU anywhere in the catalogue.
findings.evidence: ary query on AccountMaster GroupID 508 'Stiching Charges Payable' (18 tailor accounts: Anita-Tailor Rs 4.39 L, Rahul Talior Rs 3.51 L, Balwinder Singh Tailor Rs 1.54 L, Virender Singh Tailor Rs 1.44 L, Pooja, Joginder, Kuldeep Kaur, Inderpreet Kaur, Suman Kaur, Sukhdeep Kaur and 8 more). Cost by year: ary query on TransactionChild/TransactionMaster AccountID IN (2228,1922) → 2023: 205,995 / 2024: 392,532 / 2025: 576,534 / 2026-to-Aug: 358,451. Product-name search for STITCH/STICH/TAILOR/ALTERAT returns only 'Unstiched Suits' fabric SKUs, no service line.
findings.number: Rs 5.77 L (2025) cost, Rs 0 revenue, 18 tailors
findings.soWhat: The single cheapest action in this lane: the labour, the payable accounts, the fabric sales and the POS all already exist — only a service SKU and a price list are missing. Days of work, no capex, no licence.

findings.claim: ARY sells Rs 44.5 lakh a year of fabric and unstitched suits — goods that physically cannot be worn until someone stitches them — inside a Rs 2.29 crore a year clothing book.
findings.evidence: ary query grouping SaleDetail by ProductGroupMaster for 2025-08-01 onward: Unstiched Suits Rs 22,01,412 (1,088 bills) + Fabrics Rs 22,50,381 (1,871 bills) = Rs 44,51,793. Full clothing/fabric set totals Rs 2,28,96,777 across 14 groups (Academy Dress Rs 49,81,036 on 12,242 units; Winter Wear Rs 44,32,720; Footwear Rs 23,56,007).
findings.number: Rs 44.5 L/yr unstitched, Rs 2.29 Cr/yr clothing
findings.soWhat: Stitching is not a new business to invent — it is the missing second half of a Rs 44.5 L transaction ARY already completes for free, and alteration on 12,242 school-uniform units a year is a separate near-zero-cost attach as children grow.

findings.claim: Residents are hand-washing their clothes with single-use sachets and almost nobody owns an iron — the clearest unmet service need in the entire dataset.
findings.evidence: ary query on SaleDetail for detergent/fabric-care names over 12m: Rs 7,90,725 across 13,574 bills, 26,311 units, 71 SKUs. Signature items: Surf Excel Easy Wash 70 Gm — 5,915 units across 2,623 separate bills (single-wash sachets); Surf Excel Detergent Cake 84g — 2,242 units/1,172 bills; Rin Bar 250g — 827 units/605 bills. Only three 'Matic' machine-wash liquid SKUs (Rs 68k total). Separate query for IRON/PRESS: just 23 electric irons sold in 12 months (Bajaj 7, Prince 10, Havells 6) totalling Rs 17,703.
findings.number: Rs 7.91 L/yr detergent over 13,574 bills; 23 irons sold to 5,000 residents
findings.soWhat: 37 detergent transactions a day and 23 irons a year means no laundry service exists and there are almost no washing machines — a pressing counter needs Rs 60k of steam irons and no licence, and it is competing against a bucket.

findings.claim: A campus charge-account rail is already live and carries a quarter of ARY's value — 987 Akal Academy accounts plus 37 employee accounts billed Rs 2.09 crore on credit in 12 months. Services can bill straight onto it with no new payment infrastructure.
findings.evidence: ary query on SalePayment MOPID=2 joined to CustomerMaster/AccountMaster/GroupMaster for 2025-08-01 onward: Akal Academy Cs 987 customers / 4,623 bills / Rs 39,90,707; Local Debtors - Baru Sahib 12 / 4,636 / Rs 49,72,380; Employee Customer Account 37 / 837 / Rs 6,37,058; Zomato Debtors 1 / 13 / Rs 77,43,191. Total credit sale 11,019 bills, Rs 2,08,83,791, avg Rs 1,895.
findings.number: 1,024 individual campus accounts; Rs 2.09 Cr/yr on credit
findings.soWhat: The hardest part of selling services to students and staff — collecting the money — is already solved. A print job or a laundry bag can be charged to the same account number the resident already uses.

findings.claim: Himachal Pradesh has officially notified what a Lok Mitra Kendra may charge, and it covers photocopying, printing, scanning, government applications and electricity bill collection — the legal rate card for four of the services in scope.
findings.evidence: https://himseva.hp.gov.in/pages/staticSite/Rate%20List%20of%20LMK%20Charges%20for%20G2C%20Services.pdf (extracted with pdftotext -layout). '*LMK User Charges' table: G2C e-District services Rs 25/application; HPSEB Rs 5 per domestic bill, Rs 10 per commercial bill; Nakal Jamabandi Rs 10/page; G2B Rs 25/application; Scanning Rs 5/page; Black & White Page Print Rs 5/page; Color Print Rs 15/page. Per-certificate breakdown for 17 Revenue Dept certificates: Rs 20 govt fee + Rs 23.60 processing + Rs 25 LMK = Rs 68.60 total.
findings.number: Rs 25/application; Rs 5/page B&W; Rs 15/page colour; Rs 5/page scan; Rs 5/domestic electricity bill
findings.soWhat: ARY can charge Rs 5 a page for black-and-white printing with government backing, against a consumable cost near Rs 0.75 — and even pricing at Rs 2 to be fair to students leaves a ~65% margin. This converts a guess into a defensible price list.

findings.claim: A Jan Aushadhi Kendra pays 20% trade margin plus a monthly incentive of up to Rs 20,000 until Rs 5 lakh is exhausted, with an extra Rs 2 lakh for geographically disadvantaged locations — against ARY's current medicine business of just Rs 3.4 lakh a year.
findings.evidence: https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2026/mar/doc202637814101.pdf (PIB, March 2026, extracted with pdftotext): 'Operators receive a 20% trade margin on the MRP of each drug (excluding taxes)'; 'eligible for incentives of up to Rs 5.00 lakh. The incentive is provided at 20% of monthly purchases, subject to a maximum of Rs 20,000 per month and compliance with stocking requirements'; 'A minimum stocking requirement mandates that Kendras maintain at least 200 fast-moving medicines to qualify for incentives'; 'An amount of Rs. 2.00 lakhs in addition to normal incentives' for women/Divyang/SC/ST/aspirational and geographically disadvantaged regions; 18,000+ kendras, target 25,000 by March 2027. ARY baseline: ary query on Medicare product group = Rs 3,39,640 over 5,045 bills in 12m.
findings.number: 20% margin + Rs 20,000/month incentive to a Rs 5 L cap + Rs 2 L special; ARY today Rs 3.4 L/yr
findings.soWhat: Rs 57 of medicine per resident per year is implausibly low for a township with school children and elderly residents — the spend is either going 30-50 km away or through the Trust hospital. Sirmaur's hill blocks plausibly qualify for the Rs 2 L special incentive.

findings.claim: The campus empties in winter — bills swing 2.7x between the January trough and the May peak. Services must be sized on about ten effective months, and term-break travel demand is concentrated into a few weeks.
findings.evidence: ary query grouping SaleHeader by month for 2024-08 onward: Jan-2026 15,078 bills / Rs 32.5 L vs May-2026 41,388 bills / Rs 95.4 L; the same pattern repeats a year earlier (Jan-2025 10,038 bills vs Apr-2025 29,125). Full 25-month series pulled.
findings.soWhat: Any service with fixed staff or a leased machine loses money in Jan-Feb, which argues for the collection-agent model over an in-house laundry plant in year one — and makes a seasonal ticket-booking desk genuinely valuable rather than a gimmick.

findings.claim: Footfall is ~1,018 bills a day at an average of Rs 207 — the traffic a service counter would sit inside, and a basket small enough that a delivery threshold is a real lever.
findings.evidence: ary query on SaleHeader for 2025-08-22..2026-08-21: 371,721 bills, Rs 7,70,05,838 billed, Rs 207.16 average. By counter (2025-08-01 onward): Ary Pos 246,356 bills, Fruits & Vegetables 50,062, Ary G Canteen 46,173, Ary Lite 39,092, Ary Clothing 10,392.
findings.soWhat: No service here needs customer acquisition — a thousand people a day already walk in. That is why attach services beat new formats, and why the Rs 207 basket makes a Rs 400-500 free-delivery threshold worth more than the delivery fee itself.

findings.claim: Residents are already digitally self-sufficient — 46.8% of value is paid by Paytm — which kills mobile recharge as a headline service rather than supporting it.
findings.evidence: ary query on SalePayment using (Amount - ReturnAmount) for 2025-08-01 onward: Paytm (MOPID 503) 222,237 tenders / Rs 3,82,96,226 / 46.81%; Cash (MOPID 1) 166,072 / Rs 2,26,27,945 / 27.66%; Credit Sale 11,019 / Rs 2,08,83,791 / 25.53%.
findings.soWhat: A population that pays by phone recharges by phone. Recharge belongs as a free rider on a banking terminal, never as a staffed counter — this is the one candidate in the brief that the data argues against.

findings.claim: ARY's payment-mix report is wrong and overstates cash roughly 44x, because for cash tenders the Amount column stores what the customer handed over, not what was billed.
findings.evidence: 'ary sales payment-mix' reports Cash Rs 1,00,23,03,80,328 (Rs 10,023 Cr) against Rs 21 Cr of lifetime sales. Diagnosis: ary query on a real bill — SerialNumber 2264293.0015 has BillAmount 153.000 while SalePayment shows Amount 200.000, TenderAmount 200.000, ReturnAmount 47.000. True value requires Amount - ReturnAmount; digital modes (MOPID 503) carry ReturnAmount 0.
findings.number: Rs 10,023 Cr reported vs Rs 2.26 Cr actual cash
findings.soWhat: A reporting bug worth fixing in the ary CLI before anyone uses payment mix to justify a cash-handling investment — and a caution that ARY's own dashboards are not yet trustworthy for service business cases.

findings.claim: ARY already operates a B2B wholesale channel — 'Hunger Heroes', filed under a Zomato Debtors group, buys Rs 5.5-6.9 lakh at a time, about 13 times a year.
findings.evidence: ary query on SaleHeader BillAmount>100000 for 2025-08-01 onward: customer 002CM appears 13 times, Rs 4,35,378 to Rs 6,87,686 each. ary query on CustomerMaster: 002CM = 'Hunger Heroes', AccountID 4416, GroupName 'Zomato Debtors'. Also customer 0029M = 'University Students' mapped to account 'Advance From Student'.
findings.soWhat: Institutional selling is already proven here, which matters more than retail for services: exam-paper printing, a uniform-stitching contract and institutional laundry sold to the Trust would each dwarf the retail version, and a student-advance account already exists as a prepaid rail.

findings.claim: The mobile category is effectively dead — Rs 2,690 of sales on 5 bills in a year — in a township with roughly 3,000 phones and no repair shop within 30-50 km.
findings.evidence: ary query grouping SaleDetail by ProductGroupMaster for 2025-08-01 onward: Mobile group = 5 bills, Rs 2,690. For contrast: Personal Care Rs 54,55,221 / 40,604 bills; Stationary Rs 14,87,845 / 21,600 bills; Accessories Rs 11,95,871.
findings.soWhat: Screen and battery repair plus the accessory merchandise that rides with it is greenfield — and the accessory half may be the bigger prize precisely because the category is currently at zero.

findings.claim: UClean, the largest Indian laundry franchise, publishes an average store revenue of Rs 1.80 lakh a month at 30-40% gross margin with a 12-18 month payback — the closest external benchmark for a laundry unit.
findings.evidence: https://www.ucleanlaundry.com/franchise — '₹180K+' average monthly store revenue, '30-40%' average gross profit margin, '12-18 months' payback, '900+ Franchise Worldwide'. Verified as the franchisor's own published claim, not an independent audit; investment fee, royalty and per-kg pricing are not disclosed on the page.
findings.number: Rs 1.80 L/month revenue, 30-40% GM, 12-18 month payback
findings.soWhat: A captive 5,000-person campus with no competing laundry and no washing machines should reach at least a typical open-market store's revenue — which is why I size laundry at Rs 1.2 L/month conservatively rather than the Rs 1.8 L benchmark.

findings.claim: Commission rates for AePS/DMT, courier franchises, mobile recharge, IRCTC agency and the India Post franchise scheme could not be verified — the session's web-search budget was exhausted before this task began, and the operators do not publish slabs.
findings.evidence: WebSearch returned 'this session has used its web search budget (200 of 200 WebSearch calls)' on the first attempt. Fallback channels failed: NPCI (403 on /what-we-do/aeps/product-overview and JS-gated), DuckDuckGo HTML and lite (CAPTCHA), Mojeek (403), Bing RSS (topic-collapses on multi-word queries and at one point returned unrelated adult-site results). Operator homepages fetched — spicemoney.com, digitalgraminseva.in/home/AEPS, aepsindia.com, csc.gov.in — all confirm the services exist but state no rates; aepsindia.com only says commissions 'vary'. India Post franchise scheme pages 404 on the rebuilt indiapost.gov.in portal.
findings.soWhat: The five services sized purely on my own priors (banking correspondent Rs 10.5k/mo, courier Rs 14.5k/mo, tickets Rs 18k/mo, recharge Rs 5.7k/mo) together account for only Rs 48.6k of Rs 3.22 L monthly gross profit — 15%. The four verified-anchor services carry 85% of the case, so the unverified rates do not change the recommendation, only the tail.

findings.claim: Baru Sahib's existing infrastructure was not checked: whether the township already has a bank branch, ATM, post office, institutional laundry, a Trust pharmacy or a registered pharmacist.
findings.evidence: No ARY table records these, and I did not attempt to contact the Trust or verify PIN 173101 facility listings. The 'ary' CLI reads only ARY's own FusionERP database.
findings.soWhat: This is the largest single risk to the sizing. An existing hostel laundry removes Rs 54k/month, a Trust dispensary removes Rs 36k/month, and an on-campus bank removes the banking-correspondent case entirely. One conversation with the Trust administrator resolves all of it and should precede any capex.

recommendations.action: Bill the stitching ARY already pays for. Create a 'Services' product group and a stitching/alteration SKU, publish a price list (tailor job-rate + ~50%, alterations Rs 40-80), and open a service revenue account in the chart of accounts. The 18 tailors, their payable accounts, the Rs 44.5 L/yr fabric book and the POS all already exist — nothing needs buying. Estimated Rs 87,000/month revenue at ~Rs 34,500 gross profit.
recommendations.blocker: Confirm with the ARY accountant whether Academy Dress and stitched-garment selling prices already absorb the tailors' cost. If they do, separating it out is a re-labelling and only the markup plus alterations is genuinely incremental — still worth doing for visibility, but size it down.

recommendations.action: Instrument services before selling any. Add a Direct/Indirect Income account per service line and a 'Services' product group in FusionERP, and start using the POS's existing per-payment-mode commission_pct field (currently 0.000 on all 11 modes). Without this, every service below is invisible in the books exactly as tailoring has been for three years.

Open a document counter at Ary Lite: photocopy, printing, scanning, spiral/comb binding, lamination and passport photos. Price black-and-white at Rs 2/page — well under the Rs 5 that Himachal officially notifies for a Lok Mitra Kendra — with colour at Rs 15 and scanning at Rs 5. ~Rs 1.5 L capex, no licence, and Stationary already does Rs 14.9 L/yr over 21,600 bills, so the customers are provably at the counter. Estimated Rs 1,10,000/month revenue at ~Rs 77,000 gross profit; payback about two to three months.
recommendations.blocker: none — but ask the Akal Academy office who prints their exam papers today; that single B2B contract could be larger than all retail printing combined.

recommendations.action: Start a pressing and wash-and-fold collection counter — the highest-confidence unmet need in the data. Two industrial steam irons, tables, racks and a token system for about Rs 60,000, at Rs 15-20 per garment pressed and Rs 70/kg wash-and-fold. Justified by Rs 7.91 L/yr of detergent across 13,574 bills, 5,915 single-wash sachets, and just 23 electric irons sold to 5,000 people in a year. Defer the Rs 8-12 L in-house washing plant until the collection volumes are real. Estimated Rs 1,20,000/month revenue at ~Rs 54,000 gross profit.
recommendations.blocker: Confirm with the hostel wardens whether Akal Academy and Eternal University hostels already provide laundry inside their fees. If they do, this collapses to a staff-family and dry-cleaning service and should be resized down sharply.

recommendations.action: Launch in-campus delivery on WhatsApp with two delivery staff, priced at Rs 25 per order and waived above a Rs 400-500 basket. Sell it on basket uplift, not the fee: the average bill is Rs 207, so pulling delivery orders to a Rs 400 threshold is worth an estimated Rs 76,000/month in extra merchandise gross profit on top of ~Rs 27,000 in fee margin. Target married staff families with small children and elderly residents — the people least able to walk to the counter. The POS already carries 'Cash on Delivery' and 'Advance against Order' modes.
recommendations.blocker: Trust permission to move staff and goods around the residential township, and agreement on delivery hours

recommendations.action: Revive the mobile category with repair plus accessories — currently Rs 2,690 of sales on 5 bills a year against roughly 3,000 phones and no repair shop within 30-50 km. Bring a technician in two days a week to start, with about Rs 40,000 in tools and a screen/battery parts float. Estimated Rs 88,000/month revenue at ~Rs 32,200 gross profit, of which the accessory half is really a merchandise gap sitting at zero.
recommendations.blocker: Finding a competent technician willing to travel to Baru Sahib, or training an existing counter hand

recommendations.action: Apply for a Jan Aushadhi Kendra. Verified economics: 20% trade margin on MRP ex-tax plus 20% of monthly purchases capped at Rs 20,000/month until Rs 5 lakh is drawn, with a possible extra Rs 2 lakh because Sirmaur's hill blocks plausibly qualify as geographically disadvantaged. ARY's Medicare group does only Rs 3.4 L/yr — Rs 57 per resident per year — for a township with school children and elderly residents. Estimated Rs 80,000/month revenue at ~Rs 36,000 gross profit including the incentive.
recommendations.blocker: A registered pharmacist (B.Pharm/D.Pharm) and a drug licence. Before spending anything, establish whether the Kalgidhar Trust hospital already dispenses to residents — if it does, this is not an opportunity.

recommendations.action: Open a courier and parcel point handling both inbound collection and outbound booking. Pursue an India Post franchise outlet first, since India Post is the carrier most likely to serve PIN 173101 reliably, and add a private courier as a second rail. Estimated Rs 17,000/month revenue at ~Rs 14,500 gross profit — modest money, but it is what makes online shopping and returns usable at all from a closed township 30-50 km from a market, and every collection trip is a footfall event.
recommendations.blocker: India Post franchise commission rates and eligibility at PIN 173101 could not be verified — the scheme document is not reachable on the rebuilt indiapost.gov.in portal. Get the rate card from the Nahan or Rajgarh head post office.

recommendations.action: Run a seasonal ticket-booking desk for bus and rail, opening about six weeks before each term break. Verified seasonality justifies it: bills fall from 41,388 in May to 15,078 in January, meaning thousands of children and students travel out within a few weeks. Near-zero capex via an IRCTC authorised-agent arrangement through a principal agent plus a bus aggregator login. Estimated Rs 20,000/month averaged over the year at ~Rs 18,000 gross profit, concentrated into a few weeks.
recommendations.blocker: IRCTC agent authorisation route and the permitted service-charge cap are unverified. Also ask the school whether it books group travel — an institutional travel desk would be far larger than retail ticketing.

recommendations.action: Apply for a Lok Mitra Kendra authorisation through the HimSeva portal (the LMK login already exists there). The direct fee income is small — an estimated Rs 8,000/month at ~Rs 7,200 gross profit from Rs 25 per application and Rs 5 per domestic HPSEB bill — but it is what legitimises charging for printing and scanning at the officially notified rates and gives ARY a government-service identity in the township.
recommendations.blocker: Whether an LMK allotment is available for the Rajgarh block of Sirmaur, and whether a Lok Mitra Kendra already operates nearby

recommendations.action: Sign up as a banking correspondent for AePS cash-out and domestic money transfer with one partner (Spice Money, PayNearby, Fino or IPPB) — a UIDAI-certified biometric device costs Rs 2,000-3,500. The strategic case beats the revenue case: ARY takes in Rs 2.26 Cr of cash a year that must be physically banked from a hill campus, and cash-out converts that till cash into bank balance while earning commission. Estimated Rs 11,000/month revenue at ~Rs 10,450 gross profit, plus real goodwill with non-teaching staff who need to remit money home.
recommendations.blocker: Establish first whether Baru Sahib already has a bank branch or ATM inside the township — if it does, drop this. Also weigh AePS fraud liability and the Trust's view on cash handling.

recommendations.action: License a cobbler and a cycle repairer a pitch outside the counter on a revenue share rather than putting them on ARY's payroll — zero capex, zero payroll risk, an estimated Rs 5,000/month to ARY, and high resident goodwill against 5,059 pairs of footwear a year sold onto hill terrain.

Fix the ary CLI's payment-mix report before anyone builds a business case on it. It overstates cash roughly 44x (Rs 10,023 Cr against Rs 21 Cr of lifetime sales) because it sums SalePayment.Amount, which for cash tenders holds what the customer handed over rather than what was billed. Correct value is Amount minus ReturnAmount.

openQuestions: Does Baru Sahib township already have a bank branch, ATM, post office or India Post outlet inside it? This single answer decides the banking-correspondent and courier recommendations. Ask the Trust administrator or the ARY counter manager.

Do the Akal Academy and Eternal University hostels already provide laundry as part of their fees, and who does it? This is the largest swing factor in the whole sizing — Rs 54,000/month of estimated gross profit rests on the answer. Ask the hostel wardens.

Is the Rs 5.77 lakh/year of stitching cost already recovered inside Academy Dress and garment selling prices, or genuinely absorbed as a Direct Expense against margin? Determines whether billing stitching separately is new revenue or a re-labelling. Ask the ARY accountant to trace one uniform SKU's price build-up.

Does the Kalgidhar Trust hospital or dispensary already supply medicines to residents, and is a registered pharmacist available on campus? Decides whether the Jan Aushadhi Kendra is an opportunity or a duplication. Ask the Trust medical officer.

Who prints Akal Academy's exam papers, worksheets and school stationery today, and at what annual cost? A single institutional print contract could exceed all retail photocopying combined. Ask the school office.

Would the Trust permit cash-handling (AePS), a pharmacy and a laundry inside a closed religious township, and are there restrictions on outside vendors on campus? Ask Trust management before any capex.

What are the India Post Franchise Outlet commission rates per article and the security deposit, and is PIN 173101 eligible? Could not be verified — the scheme document 404s on the rebuilt indiapost.gov.in portal. Ask the Nahan or Rajgarh head post office directly.

What does a specific BC partner actually pay per AePS withdrawal and per DMT remittance in 2026? No operator publishes slabs. Get written quotes from Spice Money, PayNearby, Fino and IPPB and compare.
What is IRCTC's permitted agent service charge per ticket today, and what is the cheapest route to authorised-agent status for a non-travel business? Ask an IRCTC principal agent / RSP.

Is 'Hunger Heroes' (Rs 77.4 lakh a year, filed under Zomato Debtors) a campus food-delivery operation? If so, ARY's proposed delivery staff could serve it too, and the two should be planned together. Ask the Basement counter manager.

How many of the ~5,000 residents are HP-domiciled? This sets the real ceiling on Lok Mitra Kendra certificate volume, which I could only guess at 1,200-1,500. Ask the Academy and University registrars.

Is there mains water, drainage and reliable three-phase power at the counter for a future in-house laundry, and what does power cost? ARY's Electricity Expense is Rs 8.39 lakh — ask the ARY site manager before committing to Phase B.
